_comment: CloudFront response headers policy for the PNSM frontends.
aws cloudfront create-response-headers-policy \
--cli-input-json file://deploy/cloudfront-response-headers-policy.json
The id it returns goes into ResponseHeadersPolicyId in
deploy/cloudfront-distribution.json.
WHY NOT JUST THE nginx HEADERS?
Because for the SPA there is no nginx. The bundle is served from S3 through
CloudFront, and S3 returns exactly the headers stored on the object -- it
has no notion of a security policy. deploy/nginx.conf.template covers the
case where a frontend runs as an ECS task behind an ALB (staging, and
Person 2's dashboard if it ever needs an origin); this policy covers the
S3+CloudFront path. Both exist because both paths exist, and a header set
on only one of them is a header an attacker simply routes around.
OWASP A02, master plan: Content-Security-Policy default-src 'self' and
X-Frame-Options DENY.
The CSP here is the same policy as the nginx template. Keep them in step:
tests/security/test_headers_parity.py fails if they drift.
SHAPE: create-response-headers-policy takes
{"ResponseHeadersPolicyConfig": {...}}, not the config fields at the top
level.

ResponseHeadersPolicyConfig.Name: pnsm-frontend-security-headers
ResponseHeadersPolicyConfig.Comment: OWASP A02 headers for the PNSM SPA served from S3

ContentSecurityPolicy.ContentSecurityPolicy: default-src 'self'; base-uri 'self'; form-action 'self'; frame-ancestors 'none'; object-src 'none'; script-src 'self'; style-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline'; img-src 'self' data: blob: https:; font-src 'self' data:; connect-src 'self' <API_ORIGIN> <S3_ORIGIN>; worker-src 'self' blob:; upgrade-insecure-requests

_comment_hsts: Two years with preload. Preload is a one-way door -- browsers ship the
list in their binaries and removal takes months -- so it is set only
once the custom domain is final. Until then, drop Preload to false.

_comment: X-XSS-Protection: 0. Not a typo and not laziness. The legacy XSS
auditor it enables was removed from every modern browser and, while it
existed, introduced its own information-disclosure bugs. Explicitly
disabling it is current OWASP guidance; the CSP above is the real
control.
camera and geolocation are granted to self because the check-in flow
is the entire product. Everything else is denied outright, so a
compromised third-party script cannot reach a sensor the app never
uses.
Items.Value: accelerometer=(), camera=(self), geolocation=(self), gyroscope=(), magnetometer=(), microphone=(), payment=(), usb=()

_comment: S3 stamps every response with x-amz-request-id and x-amz-id-2. They are
useful in a support ticket and useless to a browser, and they confirm
the storage backend to anyone running curl. Stripped at the edge.
